set.answer: Keep atomic reservation in the same transaction and Reserved -> FundingPlanned -> Funded. Replace the fixed 2% default with a sponsor-set buffer per pool calibrated from a stress model (e.g. high-percentile net outflow over the settlement horizon plus December peak), with 2% allowed only as an explicitly labeled placeholder until 12 months of data exist. Fix percentage grants at approval (the amount that is reserved, communicated and expensed), with an option to re-fix only by a new approval.
set.conservative_fallback: Per-grant liquidation with T+settlement funding when the buffer is breached; block the grant at FundingPlanned until cash settles.
set.remaining_uncertainty: Actual outflow distributions per sponsor/pool; whether any sponsor IPS forbids cash sleeves; donor expectation for percentage grants.
acceptance_criteria: Given two concurrent grant approvals that together exceed fund capacity, when both commit, then exactly one succeeds and the other is rejected with no over-reservation.

Given a pool with buffer policy version v, when buffer cash falls below the configured floor, then a replenishment trade instruction is generated and an alert raised, and the policy version is recorded on the event.
Given a percentage grant of 10% approved when fund value is $50,000, when market value changes before payment, then the payable remains $5,000.
Given no stress calibration exists for a pool, when the buffer default is displayed, then it is labeled 'placeholder - not calibrated'.
reconsideration_triggers: Two or more buffer breaches in a quarter

set.activation_gate: Sponsor investment committee (or board) approval of the liquidity/buffer policy within the investment policy statement.

(b) Stress-calibrated buffer (recommended): modest analytics cost, low friction, low exposure. (c) Per-grant liquidation: no cash drag but trade cost, settlement delay and ops friction; loses same-day grant payment.

Given an agency fund charged a fee for March, when March closes unpaid, then fee revenue and a receivable are recognized in March.
Given a grant recognized as payable, when the daily fee base is computed, then the payable amount is excluded.

If an ACH/card payment is later returned or charged back, reverse the contribution (it was never completed) and void/amend the acknowledgment; this is not a 'refund' of an accepted asset. Given DTC shares credited to the sponsor account on Jan 2 after a Dec 30 instruction, when acknowledged, then the gift date is Jan 2 and the instruction date is retained.
Given an ACH gift returned R10 on day 40, when the return posts, then the contribution and capacity are reversed and the acknowledgment is voided or amended.

set.answer: Treatments: (1) Contribution without donor restrictions - transfer instrument explicitly grants variance power, no donor redirect/refund right, no time/purpose restriction beyond advisory privileges. (2) Contribution with donor restrictions - instrument imposes time (incl. perpetual) or purpose restriction the sponsor treats as binding (variance power does not remove perpetual endowment restrictions per Boston practice). (3) Liability (agency) - resource provider names itself or affiliate as beneficiary (REGARDLESS of variance power), or provider retains redirect/revocation/refund right, or controls the recipient. (4) Equity transaction - financially interrelated entities naming themselves. Missing variance-power evidence blocks (1).
set.conservative_fallback: Classify as liability any program where variance power evidence is missing or donor retains redirect/refund rights, pending CPA review.
set.remaining_uncertainty: Current ASC paragraph numbers for FAS 136 content (958-605-25-24 cross-reference seen in ASU 2018-08; others unverified); sponsor-specific auditor judgments on designated funds.

Given a workplace program allowing donors to redirect or refund, when classified, then treatment is Liability.
Given a DAF program version lacking a stored variance-power clause, when a contribution posts, then posting as unrestricted contribution is blocked.
Given a perpetual endowment gift with variance power, when classified, then treatment is With Donor Restrictions.

set.activation_gate: Sponsor counsel/CPA review of each program's transfer-instrument wording (variance power and beneficiary terms).

set.answer: Confirm the architecture rule, with a sharper test: the operator stays outside federal MSB and state money-transmission definitions if (a) it never receives or holds donor/grant money (no operator, FBO, or pooled accounts), (b) it has no ability to unilaterally execute or indefinitely prevent a payment (sponsor-held bank/custodian credentials and approval; operator software only relays sponsor-authorized instructions), and (c) donor payments settle directly into sponsor-owned accounts through BSA-regulated processors/banks. Replace the gate 'multistate memo before embedded/white-label that touches money' with: a recorded FundsFlow conformance check against tests (a)-(c) plus a jurisdiction table (federal, MTMA states, CA, NY, TX, FL, others default-conservative). External legal authorization is required only for a deployment that fails (a)-(c): then use a licensed money transmitter or bank partner, or obtain licences.
set.conservative_fallback: Operate only models where all money moves between donor/sponsor/grantee accounts at BSA-regulated institutions under sponsor credentials; for any embedded host, contractually prohibit the host from receiving funds (or require host to be licensed/agent-of-payee of the sponsor under a written agreement satisfying MTMA §3.01(b)/CA §2010(l)).
set.remaining_uncertainty: No regulator ruling addresses a DAF software operator with instruction-only authority specifically. Non-MTMA, non-surveyed states may define transmission more broadly. Treatment of an operator acting as ACH third-party sender or holding API payment-initiation credentials is unsettled. Texas statute text was read only via bill analysis; California statute via mirror (official site blocked).
acceptance_criteria: Given any deployment, When its FundsFlow declaration is saved, Then every account holding contribution or grant money shows the sponsor (or custodian for the sponsor) as title holder and no operator/affiliate account appears; otherwise activation is blocked.

Given an operator service account, When it attempts to initiate a payment from a sponsor account without a sponsor approval record or sponsor-authorized standing policy, Then the request is rejected and logged.
Given operator billing, When fees are charged, Then they are invoiced to the sponsor and never netted from contributions or grants.

Given an embedded host, When the host integration is configured, Then donor payments settle directly to the sponsor's merchant/bank account and the host contract records that the host does not receive funds (or records host licence/agent-of-payee agreement).
Given a change to FundsFlow, When saved, Then the conformance check and jurisdiction table review re-run before activation.
reconsideration_triggers: Any proposal for operator-held, FBO, pooled, or settlement accounts, or netting of fees from charitable money
Operator obtaining payment-initiation credentials usable without sponsor approval, or acting as ACH third-party sender
Expansion to a state not in the jurisdiction table or whose MTMA version changes
New FinCEN ruling/guidance or state regulator action on software platforms or charitable payment facilitation
Embedded host or white-label partner that collects donor funds
set.external_authorization_required: None for a deployment that passes the no-receipt/no-unilateral-control tests. For any deployment where the operator or its affiliate receives or controls funds: state money-transmitter licences (via NMLS) and FinCEN MSB registration, or an executed agreement with a licensed transmitter/bank acting for the sponsor.
set.activation_gate: None for a deployment that passes the no-receipt/no-unilateral-control tests. For any deployment where the operator or its affiliate receives or controls funds: state money-transmitter licences (via NMLS) and FinCEN MSB registration, or an executed agreement with a licensed transmitter/bank acting for the sponsor.
set.alternative_design: A) Instruction-only relay (recommended): cost low, friction moderate (sponsor approval steps, sponsor-held credentials), exposure low, lost opportunity: no operator float income, no instant cross-sponsor settlement. B) Partner with licensed processor/transmitter for donor collection (e.g., processor as agent of payee of sponsor): cost per-transaction fees, friction low, exposure shifted to licensee, lost opportunity small. C) Obtain money-transmitter licences (~multistate NMLS, bonds, net worth, audits): high cost and 12-24 months, enables float and settlement products; not justified for release 1. D) Agent-of-payee structure where operator receives funds as sponsor's agent: legally available in MTMA states and CA (charitable services covered), but NY/FL lack a clean statutory equivalent and operator would carry custody/insolvency risk; reject for release 1.

Operator-maintained pools remain prohibited as policy (operator status risk).

Policy controls: risk-based identity proofing for advisory-privilege holders, successors, and anyone granted payment-related authority; OFAC screening of donors, advisors, successors, grantees and payors of contributions at onboarding, on list updates, and before each grant; a written sanctions compliance program per OFAC Framework components for the sponsor, supported by platform logs. Change source-of-funds review from threshold-only to risk-based: complex assets, contributions above a sponsor threshold, AND pattern triggers below threshold (rapid in-out, third-party payors, structuring-like splits, high-risk geographies).
set.conservative_fallback: Adopt CIP-equivalent identity verification (name, DOB, address, ID number, documentary/non-documentary verification) for all advisory-privilege holders and payors above threshold.
set.remaining_uncertainty: Full BSA 'financial institution' list (31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2)) not fetched; bank/custodian contractual KYC expectations vary.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new advisory-privilege holder or successor, When activated, Then identity proofing evidence is recorded.
Given any party (donor, advisor, successor, grantee, payor), When onboarded or before each grant, Then OFAC screening against the current SDN list is run and recorded with list version.
Given contributions below threshold, When pattern rules (third-party payor, rapid grant-out, split contributions) fire, Then a source-of-funds review case opens.
Given an OFAC list update, When published, Then all active parties are rescreened within the sponsor-set window.
reconsideration_triggers: Operator or affiliate becomes MSB, RIA or BD
New FinCEN rule covering nonprofits or platforms
set.alternative_design: A) Risk-based identity proofing + universal OFAC screening (recommended): moderate cost (IDV vendor per check), low friction for small donors. B) Full CIP-equivalent for everyone: higher cost and abandonment. C) Rely on bank KYC only: lowest cost, leaves donors/advisors unverified and OFAC exposure on grants.

set.answer: No report is legally required. Keep evidence engineering from inception. Make SOC 2 description/CUEC/audit-period work conditional on (a) a contract or counterparty demanding a report, or (b) a second user entity. Before go-live, obtain the sponsor auditor's written planned approach (SOC 1 type 2, direct testing, or substantive) and size SOC 1 timing from that, not from sponsor count.
set.conservative_fallback: Commission a SOC 1 type 2 (ledger and ITGC objectives) for the first full period after go-live, and a SOC 2 type 1 readiness assessment; costs per bearer map.
set.remaining_uncertainty: Exact AU-C 402 wording not fetched (gated); relied on converged ISA 402. The auditor's planned reliance strategy is unknown.
acceptance_criteria: Given R1 with no SOC report, when the sponsor auditor plans the audit, then a written planned approach (report, direct testing or substantive) is recorded in the assurance register before production cutover.
Given a counterparty contract requiring SOC 2, when the contract is executed, then SOC 2 description and CUEC work items are created automatically.
Given any control in the register, when evidence is requested for a period, then the system produces complete population evidence with integrity hashes and flags missing evidence.
reconsideration_triggers: Second user entity (sponsor or partner) onboarded.
Sponsor auditor states it will require a SOC 1.
Bank, custodian or payment-processor contract requires SOC 2.
Unbound begins to hold or move funds.
set.external_authorization_required: Sponsor's external auditor's documented planned approach to Unbound as service organization (engagement planning memo or written confirmation); any counterparty contract clause requiring a SOC report.
set.activation_gate: Sponsor's external auditor's documented planned approach to Unbound as service organization (engagement planning memo or written confirmation); any counterparty contract clause requiring a SOC report.
set.alternative_design: (A) Sponsor-titled reconciliation: daily automated reconciliation of the ledger to custodian/bank files that the sponsor receives directly makes a substantive audit feasible. Cost: low build. Friction: low. Exposure: auditor may still test ITGCs. Lost opportunity: none. (B) Right-to-audit clause plus a standing ITGC evidence pack for direct testing. Cost: auditor hours billed to sponsor (~tens of hours). (C) Early SOC 1 type 2. Cost: highest (typically five-to-six-figure annual fee plus a 6-12 month observation period, industry estimate, unverified). Exposure: lowest. Prefer A+B in R1, C when more than one user entity or a contract requires it.

set.answer: No sponsor-maintained investment pools are offered (OD-M-07). Each sponsor delegates investment management to an external registered investment manager or custodian platform (e.g. Schwab) under a written agreement and keeps the duties to select, scope and monitor it; donors recommend allocations among the manager's options. Research finding retained for reference: sponsor-maintained pools, including multi-sponsor pools, would be lawful under ICA §3(c)(10)(B) with §7(e) disclosure, but would need a new owner decision.
set.superseded_answer: Legal basis per pool: ICA §3(c)(10)(B) (exclusion), Securities Act §3(a)(4) (exempt security), Exchange Act §3(e) (sponsor not a broker/dealer, subject to §3(e)(2)), Advisers Act §203(b)(4) (sponsor personnel advice) plus registered adviser for any external manager, ICA §7(e) donor disclosure. Multi-sponsor pools ARE permitted by the statute when maintained by a 501(c)(3) sponsor (host sponsor as trustee/administrator or with removal power) and holding only charitable organizations' assets. Keep release 1 single-sponsor as a business-policy choice (operational simplicity), but record multi-sponsor host-sponsor pools as a legally available release-2 option rather than prohibited. Operator-maintained pools remain prohibited as policy (operator status risk).

set.answer: Answered by XID-INV-003 (OD-M-07): multi-sponsor pools would be lawful under §3(c)(10)(B)(i), but no sponsor-maintained pools are offered; investment management is delegated to an external manager.
set.superseded_answer: Yes, under the statutory text: §3(c)(10)(B)(i) covers funds of 'one or more charitable organizations' maintained by a charitable organization, and 'maintained' includes serving as trustee/administrator or holding removal power. Conditions: only charitable-organization assets, §7(e) disclosure, §3(e)(2) compensation limit. Keep disabled in release 1 as business policy.
